resources.string: A qualitative view of normal human epidermis. Sizes, timing, and paths are schematic; pigment distribution varies, and the transfer shown is one proposed route.
A melanocyte sits in the basal layer of the epidermis. Its branching dendrites reach between neighboring keratinocytes.
Inside the melanocyte, melanin is made and accumulates in membrane-bound compartments called melanosomes.
Some melanosomes move from the cell body along the dendrites toward their tips, bringing pigment close to keratinocytes.

One proposed route is shown: the melanocyte releases a melanin core, and a keratinocyte takes it up. Other proposed routes involve membrane-wrapped pigment packets or uptake of part of a dendrite tip.
Pigment can remain dispersed in a keratinocyte or gather over the nucleus on the side facing the skin surface. This cap can reduce UV reaching nuclear DNA, but it does not block all UV.
Tarafder et al. (2014): Melanin release and uptake
Kobayashi et al. (1998): Melanin caps and UV effects on DNA
